newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Ganz Tech in China gold deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Ganz Tech in China gold deal.

text.p: Ganz Technologies Bhd said on Wednesday it has entered into an agreement to acquire a 50 percent stake in China's Harbin Classic Mines Machinery Ltd Co.
Ganz said in a statement that it will subscribe to two million new shares in Harbin Classic for a total of $2 million and would advance up to $2 million to Harbin as working capital.
The financing of the proposed investment will be through internally generated funds and bank borrowings, Ganz said.
Harbin Classic has concessions to mine for gold at two sites in the Ganzi Tibetan autonomous region, west of Sichuan province in China, Ganz said.
The mines are estimated to have extractable reserves of eight tons of gold, which Harbin Classic "believes it will be able to fully extract within a three-year period", Ganz said.
The 50 percent stake in Harbin Classic will result in additional earnings to Ganz of $8.8 million per year which amounts to an additional 1.11 ringgit per share, Ganz said.
For the six months ended June 30, 1996, Ganz reported a net profit of 657,000 ringgit or 3.32 cents a share.
Ganz, a glove maker, said the proposed investment would enable it to reduce dependence on its core latex glove business "which is becoming increasingly competitive".
Ganz's stock was suspended on February 14 at the company's request. The stock last traded at 19.60 ringgit prior to the suspension.
